summary: @brick-v2/icons exfiltrates CI/cloud credentials via native addon on require
details: The package's main entry (index.js) unconditionally loads a prebuilt native addon at prebuilds/<platform>-<arch>/metrics.node inside a try/catch on module import. The ELF binary reads credential-grade environment variables from the installer's process (AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, AWS_SESSION_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN, NPM_TOKEN, NODE_AUTH_TOKEN, SYSTEM_ACCESSTOKEN, ACTIONS_RUNTIME_TOKEN, ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN) along with host fingerprint fields (package name, hostname, user, OS, architecture, release, cwd, full env block) and transmits them via a raw-socket HTTP/1.0 POST to the hardcoded host oob.s4yhii.com at path /native. The native code calls fork()+setsid() to detach from the parent Node process, allowing exfiltration to continue after the require() returns. An icon package has no legitimate need for a native addon, and the version number 999.0.2 under the @brick-v2 scope is characteristic of dependency-confusion overshoot targeting internal package resolution. The destination host is unrelated to any plausible first-party infrastructure for an icon library.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
